blocks.x: For each pitfall, ask what evidence or decision is missing, who owns it, and what the smallest corrective step is.

Glean's onboarding training highlights a pitfall that happens before the Blueprint starts. Teams that lack confidence in the process present it as a burden, and customers decline. The fix is to position it consultatively, as a structured way to find where AI will matter most, and to show what the customer gets at the end.

blocks.title: Common Blueprint pitfalls
blocks.alt: Six cards naming common Blueprint pitfalls: pitching the Blueprint apologetically, Visioning without prioritization, DITL skipped before a trial, value claimed without baselines, a readout with no decision, and a pilot with no success criteria.

items.label: Pilot without criteria
items.detail: A test with no path to a decision

practice.x: Diagnose this situation: three Visioning sessions have produced 40 use cases, but no business owner has prioritized any of them.

worked.x: This is the wishlist pitfall. Run a scoring session with the business owners to select a small set of hero use cases. Each hero needs an owner, an outcome, and a target, and the rest stay in a backlog.
Confirm the hero choices with the sponsor before scheduling DITL interviews.
